about: Design recipe ledger for all mockups. Newest entries FIRST. Before building any mockup: run `node ledger-check.js` (or read the last 10 entries) — any displayFont, paletteFamily, or loaderConcept used in the last 10 entries is OFF the table for the new build. After building: append the new entry in the same commit as the mockup. Backfilled entries (pre 2026-06-09) have null block codes because the data wasn't recorded at build time.

entries.archetype: A/C hybrid modern-industrial, BRIGHT build (white page + cool stone cards; ink #16191d strictly PANEL duty: trust strip, cta band, footer)
entries.paletteFamily: BRIGHT WHITE page + cool stone #f2f4f6 + CRANE YELLOW #edb200 single working accent at PLANT-SIGNAGE register: every yellow surface carries INK text like machine livery (CTAs, FAB, nav CTA, form button, home chip, hero badge icons, review stars, svc top-borders, the H1 beam-rule under 'London', the loader hook and bolts), deep #8a6400 for mono labels ON WHITE, pale #ffd35c for small type ON INK (legibility split), #c99400 hover. INK #16191d strictly panel duty (trust strip, cta band, footer; the page ground stays white and the fold is white both viewports). Argued vs the window's three golds: paul-marchant TORCH GOLD #e3aa32 is a flame register carrying white-text CTAs on a full lead-black ground; jbc ANTIQUE BRASS #c39a5e is a desaturated heirloom metal on midnight ink; jmcf PINE HONEY #b96a12 is a dark timber amber at ~40% lightness whose CTAs are white-text. Crane yellow is ~47deg at ~55% lightness and FULL chroma on a WHITE page with BLACK-text signage CTAs, a machine-plant register not a flame, metal-object or timber one (the gilt-vs-machine-yellow same-family-different-register precedent applied in reverse). Argued vs dedee-construction, the window's other STEEL FIXING build (same trade, same city): that is blued cobalt #2545cf working accent on white with mill-scale graphite fold posters and rebar-oxide bar props; this build touches no blue, no graphite fold (white fold both viewports) and no oxide, and its motif is a skyline not a cage. Blues/greens/teals/reds/oranges/navies untouched. Story: the page is the drawing the engineer signed, and the yellow is the crane that lands the steel in it
entries.loaderConcept: Beam Lift (crane-family RE-EXECUTION of ld-cranelift, first used mcv-full-construction, outside the 10-window; not a replay): ld-cranelift draws a crane that lowers the BRAND BLOCK onto a datum; this one rigs a STRUCTURAL I-BEAM in elevation. On white, an ink tower-crane jib draws itself with lattice bracing (0.05-0.6s), two ink columns fade up, a crane-yellow hook line drops from the jib carrying an ink I-beam (two flanges + web, 0.7-1.55s cubic overshoot) and lands it across the columns, then two yellow bolt heads pop at the bearings (1.6/1.72s) and the Chakra Petch NANEK ENGINEERING wordmark rises beneath; mono ticks SLUNG / LIFTED / LANDED / BOLTED. 2.2s JS teardown + 2.9s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.6s, reduced-motion static landed beam + brand. Hands off INTO the fold BOTH viewports: the hero's drawn London-skyline band (silhouette towers + a tower crane) receives the SAME yellow beam dropping in at 2.0s next to its crane, the Shard's yellow beacon blinks on a 3.2s loop, and the H1's yellow beam-rule under 'London' draws at 2.05s on the same register. Distinct from every loader in the window (panes reveal a photograph, bricks knock through, a ladder drops from a hatch, a dome seam gets torch-welded, a house elevation builds, colour chips fan and flood, a badge rises from the ground, drains lay and run, ground rebuilds in strata, rebar cages get tied and poured over): dedee's ld-cagepour is the same trade but ties a REINFORCEMENT MAT flat in plan and buries it in concrete; this rigs ONE structural beam in elevation from a crane and bolts it, erection not reinforcement, and the skyline handoff is its own

Argued vs the two black-and-gold builds that landed the SAME DAY: paul-marchant-lead-roofing is a full-dark lead-graphite #101214 ground with TORCH GOLD #e3aa32 (~42deg, a flame, a light-source register) and jbc-homes-developments is a full-dark midnight ink #0e1016 with ANTIQUE BRASS #c39a5e (~36deg at ~57% lightness, a desaturated heirloom metal). This build inverts both on the axis that matters most: the PAGE IS WHITE and the dark never carries the fold on desktop, the accent is ~31deg at ~40% lightness and full chroma, and it is a MATERIAL-TIMBER register, pine and chipboard, not a metal or a flame (the gilt-vs-machine-yellow same-family-different-register precedent applied across ~5-11deg of hue plus a value drop). Argued vs ollerton-plant-civils, the window's other warm accent: drain orange #dd5c14 sits ~21deg at high chroma on a stone POSTER page with no dark panel anywhere; pine honey is 10deg gold-side, darker, and this build does run a dark panel. No timber/honey accent on a white page anywhere in the window. Blues/greens/teals/reds/navies untouched. Story: the page is the new board, the dark is the loft before he gets there, and the honey is the pine ladder he leaves in it
entries.loaderConcept: Ladder Drop (NEW concept, added to loader-lab as ld-ladderdrop): the ceiling line draws across, the hatch unlatches and swings down on its hinge, a three section timber ladder telescopes out of the opening one section at a time and the feet land on the floor line, warm light spills down through the hole, and the JMCF wordmark rises up out of the hatch. Hands off INTO the hero: the loader teardown adds .lit and the hero batten strikes on the same beat, so the light continues rather than vanishing (gilfillan handoff precedent). 2.35s, transform/opacity only, fail-safe teardown at 3.2s, reduced-motion drops the ladder and shows the brand card

Argued vs jbc-homes-developments, which landed the SAME DAY from a concurrent session on the same written instruction (the ollerton/ashlea same-day-same-brief precedent, diverged deliberately on every shared axis once the collision was found): jbc is a NAVY-SIDE midnight ink #0e1016 logo-lift ground carrying CREAM #f0e9db headings and a desaturated ANTIQUE-BRASS gold #c39a5e (~36deg, ~57% lightness, a logo's rule metal at heirloom register) with champagne #e9d5a9, and its gold never floods a surface; this build is a COLD-NEUTRAL graphite ground (zero hue cast, the trade's own metal) carrying PURE WHITE headings and a hotter, higher-chroma FLAME gold #e3aa32 (~42deg at ~54% lightness and roughly double the chroma, a light-source register not a metal-object one: the gilt-vs-machine-yellow precedent applied inside one hue family), plus an achromatic milled-lead prop rail jbc has no equivalent of, and the one full-gold flood at cta duty. vs the rest of the window: the only other gold is knights-flooring's pale satin champagne on a WHITE page (opposite ground), and the only other full-dark is fraser-hoehle's green-charcoal + neon LED green (opposite accent family and register). jacobs-crown (warm ink + saturated crown gilt) stays aged out. entries.loaderConcept: Lead Burn v2, dome raise & burn (NEW concept, added to loader-lab as ld-leadburn; v1, a flat two-sheet seam weld, was CUT on Patrick's review 2026-08-14 as 'not ambitious enough' and replaced same session): on near-black, a gold line draws the OGEE DOME ELEVATION (the profile of the client's own bell dome in the hero photo, 0.08-0.58s), the base line and four curved wood-roll ribs draw in lead grey (0.45-1.1s), the dome FILLS with a milled-lead gradient (0.78s), then the payoff: a torch flame climbs the centre seam bottom-to-top (SMIL animateMotion, 1.0-1.8s) welding it in a glowing gold line, and the FINIAL SPHERE pops gold on the apex with an overshoot at 1.82s, because dressing a dome and burning its seams IS the specialism the whole brief hangs on; mono status ticks SHEET CUT / DRESSED TO ROLL / SEAM BURNED / FINIAL SET, then the Marcellus 'Paul Marchant' wordmark + mono 'Specialist Lead Roofing' sub rise at 1.8s. 2.3s JS teardown + 2.9s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.6s, reduced-motion static welded dome + brand. Hands off INTO the fold BOTH viewports: on mobile the drawn dome resolves into the REAL dome photo carrying the full-bleed fold beneath it (the drawing becomes the photograph), and the H1's gold weld-rule under 'lead' draws at 2.05s on the same register. Distinct from every loader in the window (a house elevation builds in construction order, colour chips fan and flood, a video fold, drains lay and run, ground rebuilds in strata, cages tie and pour, survey stations set, steel connections detail and stamp, heat bounces, mirrors demist) and argued vs the same-day jbc ld-elevation, the nearest neighbour (also gold line-art drawing a building): jbc draws a WHOLE HOUSE front-on in construction order and lights its windows, a builder's sequence ending in handover; this draws ONE ROOF FORM in section, fills it with the trade's own metal, runs a FLAME up it and caps it with a finial, a metalworker's sequence ending in a weld, and nothing anywhere else WELDS or BURNS. vs the lab's roofing set: Slate Run cascades slates down a pitch, Rain Shed sheds rain, Re-roof strips and re-tiles; nothing draws a dome and nothing torches a seam

Stone hexes were deliberately shifted off theirs (#eaece5 vs #eef0ec) once the collision was found. vs the rest of the window: steel-sculpture RED-OXIDE PRIMER #b04a2b (~16deg) is a matte primer at working duty on white but sits browner and darker with gunmetal PANELS beside it, where this build has no dark panel at all; dedee's oxide #b5643a is PROP duty under a blue accent; psctherm heat red #e92712 and ajs embroidery red #d23a30 are both signal reds, one half of a thermal PAIR and one on a full-navy ground. No orange has held solo working duty anywhere in the window. Older orange precedent is all ORANGE-ON-DARK, which imshaw's ledger note bans by name (imshaw roadwork amber #ff6a00 on asphalt near-black, mud-monkey hi-vis on mud-charcoal, hammond flame orange, a1-bathrooms amber on #14120f); this is the opposite construction, an orange on a WHITE and PALE-STONE page with no dark ground anywhere, and all four have long aged out. jj-building-excavations' earth build (a scroll-depth strata descent through six browns with a brick-oxide accent) is avoided end to end: no brown, no earth ground, no darkening scroll. entries.loaderConcept: Run & Fall (NEW concept, added to loader-lab as ld-runfall): on sub-base stone, a drainage run gets LAID and then RUNS. Two inspection chambers rise out of the ground with an overshoot settle (0.18s and 0.34s), a drain-orange run draws itself between them at a visible FALL (0.62s), pea-gravel bedding settles under it in an eight-step stagger (1.06-1.41s), a dashed datum line and a mono FALL 1:80 marker snap on at 1.34s to show the drop, and then the payoff: water starts flowing down the run from the high chamber to the low one on an infinite loop from 1.5s, because a drain that falls the right way IS the job. Mono status ticks CHAMBERS SET / RUN LAID / BEDDED & HAUNCHED / FALL CHECKED / CONNECTED, then the Sofia Sans OLLERTON wordmark + mono 'Plant & Civils . Wigan' sub rise at 1.72s. 2.2s JS teardown + 2.8s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.6s, reduced-motion static laid-and-running drain + brand. Hands off INTO the fold BOTH viewports: the hero closes on a bordered GROUND PANEL carrying the same run, chambers, bedding and dashed datum, tagged in mono 'FOUL RUN . 150MM . FALL 1:80', its pipe drawing at 2.05s and its flow starting at 3.2s, so the loader does not vanish, it parks in the page; at 390px that panel sits directly under the CTAs and the programme rail and is fully inside the first screenful, and the H1's orange rule grows at 2.05s on the same register. Distinct from ashlea-developments' Formation, landed the same day in the same trade: that loader DIGS A SECTION AND REBUILDS IT IN STRATA (a vertical cross-section, turf/subsoil/membrane/sub-base/blacktop, geology, what the ground is made of); this one lays a single horizontal run between two objects and puts WATER through it, which is hydraulics, not geology. Distinct from the rest of the window and the lab (cages get tied and poured over, survey stations set, steel connections detailed and stamped, heat bounces off a wall, mirrors demist, floors lay, staircases build, hedges trim, fences build) and from the lab's near neighbours: Dig Out SCOOPS ground blocks away, Trench Cut opens a trench along a marking line, Jet Clear blasts sludge out of a pipe that ALREADY EXISTS. Nothing anywhere LAYS A DRAIN, and nothing CHECKS A FALL

entries.loaderConcept: Shower On (NEW, added to loader-lab as ld-showerhead): on dark navy, a chrome riser and rainfall shower head fade down into place, then sixteen pale-blue #8fd8f5 water streams fall from the head in staggered infinite loops and land ON the JJS SERVICES wordmark sitting beneath, with a soft blue pool of light blooming behind the brand where the water hits; ~1.7s to settled, 2.2s teardown + 2.5s JS failsafe, reduced-motion hides the rig and shows the brand card. PATRICK SPECIFIED THIS DIRECTLY at review: 'i dont really get the loading screen, just do a shower head with blue water coming out on to the JJS Services name'. STANDING LESSON RECORDED: this mockup burned two cleverer loaders before landing. v1 'Step Down' (bath cross-section whose near wall dropped away while a dimension counted 520mm to 40mm) was cut as 'not a major fan of the animated climbing over the bath thing'; v2 'Panel Up' (four wall panels sliding up, yellow trims drawing down the seams) was cut as 'i dont really get the loading screen'. Both were conceptually defensible and neither read at a glance. For bathroom and shower fitters the OBVIOUS LITERAL IMAGE beats the smart one: a shower, running, over the name. Panel Up is kept in loader-lab as a valid concept for panel fitters, but note the read-at-a-glance failure before reaching for it. Water is otherwise unused in the lab, the earlier DPS hot-fill attempt having been cut; this is falling rain from a fixed head rather than a filling vessel

# Design SEED — PP Contracting Limited

**Client:** Paul Salmon · PP Contracting Limited · groundworks / driveways / general construction
**Location:** Retford, Nottinghamshire (DN22 — confirm) · covers a 60-mile radius
**Phone:** 07463 293839 / WhatsApp 447463293839. Email: NOT SUPPLIED (email card omitted; confirm at onboarding).
**Logo:** NONE supplied — "PP" tile + wordmark.
**Brief:** Newly incorporated, no website, wants credibility + enquiries. Trade = groundworks, driveways
(resin-bound + tarmac + block paving), general construction, roofing, property maintenance. Client asked
for a BLUE, modern, construction-focused look with strong quote CTAs. No years / Est. date given — do NOT
invent one. Photos = STOCK (Pexels, no people, English-reading) per the no-photos brief.

## Seed
Palette:   cool site-white (#f4f7fa) + graphite ink (#0e141c) + electric cobalt (#1f53e0); deep steel-navy
           (#0b1a33) for the CTA band, why-band and footer. Client wants blue — cobalt is deliberately NOT
           the banned ocean-blue/frost-cyan/navy+amber families; navy is a structural tone, not the accent.
Type:      Khand 600/700 (display — condensed, civil-engineering/infrastructure character) + Inter (body)
           + JetBrains Mono (spec micro-tags). Clears ledger (Clash climbing x3, all last-10 fonts banned).
Signature: "ground strata" — a layered sub-base/binder/surface banding motif used on section dividers + a
           setting-out / site-plan grid backdrop behind the hero. Groundworks builds in layers; the site
           shows it. Plus a hero spec rail (mono tags: 60-MILE RADIUS / GROUNDWORKS / DRIVEWAYS).
Loader:    NEW "surface course layup" — on navy, a cross-section fills bottom-up (sub-base grey course →
           dark binder course → cobalt finished course), then a thin screed/roller bar glides across the
           top course leaving a smooth band, and the PP Contracting wordmark settles. Driveway/tarmac/
           groundworks build-up loader — distinct from the banned Dig-Out, trowel, roller, storey-stack,
           portal-frame, hazard-stripe etc. Added to loader-lab.
Voice:     short trade voice; owner Paul named naturally in About only; CTAs = "Call us" / "Get a quote"
           (Paul is the brief contact, not a public-facing personal brand → no "Call Paul").
Reviews:   NONE fabricated — newly incorporated business → "Why PP Contracting" + a clear quote process
           instead of fake reviews.
Ledger ok: Khand unused; cool-white+cobalt+steel-navy unused; surface-course-layup loader unused;
           H2-split + S4-bento + G2-masonry not in last-10 combos ✓
Blocks:    hero:H2-split / trust:T1 / services:S4-bento(7) / gallery:G2-masonry / why:process-band /
           about:after-gallery / areas / cta-band / contact:C1
